requirements.text: All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of direction indicators categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12.
The approval marking arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps.
The approval marking arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
The lamps shall bear the approval marking.
The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The lamp shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed, except that for lamps with non-replaceable light sources this requirement does not apply.
The lamp shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s), in the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s).
The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with an electronic light source control gear.
The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with a variable luminous intensity control.
The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with a secondary operating mode.
The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1.
In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
The electronic light source control gear shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer, if it is part of the lamp but not included into the lamp body.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
The approval marking shall be placed on both, the detachable lens and the main body, if the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The lamp shall be designed and constructed so that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the functions shall be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source), except that they may be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, a note shall be made within the communication document.

The lamp shall not incorporate a logo, except that on request of the applicant the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface may incorporate only one manufacturer logo build by transparent or non-transparent components provided that all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation are fulfilled.

The logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be the only logo allowed, except that on request of the applicant the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface may incorporate a logo.
The applicant shall confirm the logo incorporation by a statement (see paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f)).
The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of such a lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) does not have to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48.
The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
The direction indicator lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
A group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.

The communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure, in case a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure is produced.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear end-outline marker lamp category RM2 emitting more than the maximum value of category RM1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a direction indicator of category 2b emitting more than the maximum value of category 2a, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear fog lamp of category F2 emitting more than the maximum value of category F1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval.
The lamp shall only be equipped with light source module(s).
The lamp shall only be equipped with non-replaceable light source(s).
The lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

When the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of device shall be met.
In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The rear lamp shall have its intensities measured with the light source continuously lit, if not otherwise specified.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
In the case of category 5 and 6 direction indicators, the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined.
This requirement shall not apply to rear-registration plate illuminating lamps.
The voltage supplied at the lamp shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems), unless otherwise specified.
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
The test laboratory may require the electronic light source control gear or the variable intensity control.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction on the measured luminous intensities.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., on the reference axis (HV).

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall not exceed the maximum, specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., in no direction where the lamp is visible.

If not otherwise specified, outside the reference axis, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, outside the reference axis, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

The applicant may request an additional test to show that in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction, the maximum intensity is not more than 2.5×10-1cd.

If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously at the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
The luminous intensities shall be tested in accordance with Annex 8.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
To check these colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
Outside this field no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4.

A luminous intensity of 6.0×10¹ cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The minimum luminous intensity in cd for R1, MR or RM1 (steady) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 4×10⁰.
The maximum luminous intensity in cd when used as R1, MR or RM1 (steady) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 1.7×10¹.
The standard light distribution for R1, MR or RM1 (steady) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 8.5×10⁰.
The angles of geometric visibility for R1, MR or RM1 (steady) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be Figure A3-I Table A2- 1.
The minimum luminous intensity in cd for R2 or RM2 (variable) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 4×10⁰.
The maximum luminous intensity in cd when used as R2 or RM2 (variable) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 4.2×10¹.
The standard light distribution for R2 or RM2 (variable) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be 2.1×10¹.
The angles of geometric visibility for R2 or RM2 (variable) rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps shall be Figure A3-I Table A2- 1.
The minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 4.
The rear position lamp shall emit light of red colour.
The stop lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 7 regarding luminous intensity and standard light distribution.
The stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60×10^2 cd when used as specified in paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b).
The stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have a standard light distribution of 1.30×10^2 cd.
The stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have angles of geometric visibility of 3×10^-1.
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a maximum luminous intensity of 7.30×10^2 cd when used as specified in paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b).
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a standard light distribution of 3.65×10^2 cd.
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have angles of geometric visibility of 3×10^-1.
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 7×10^-2 cd when used during the day.
The stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 7×10^-2 cd when used during the night.
The stop lamp of category S3 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 2.5×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S3 (steady) shall have a maximum luminous intensity of 1.10×10^2 cd when used as specified in paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b).
The stop lamp of category S3 (steady) shall have a standard light distribution of 5.5×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S3 (steady) shall have angles of geometric visibility of 3×10^-1.
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 2.5×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have a maximum luminous intensity of 1.60×10^2 cd when used as specified in paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b).
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have a standard light distribution of 8.0×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have angles of geometric visibility of 3×10^-1.
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 7×10^-2 cd when used during the day.
The stop lamp of category S4 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 7×10^-2 cd when used during the night.
The stop lamp of category MS (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4.0×10^1 cd.
The stop lamp of category MS (steady) shall have a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60×10^2 cd when used as specified in paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b).
The stop lamp of category MS (steady) shall have a standard light distribution of 1.30×10^2 cd.
The stop lamp of category MS (steady) shall have angles of geometric visibility of 3×10^-1.
The stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility as specified in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall emit light of the colour red.
The reversing lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 10 regarding luminous intensity and standard light distribution.

When the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards where a photometric value of at least 2.5×10¹ cd shall be satisfied.
The condition regarding verification up to an angle of 30° inwards for a pair of devices shall be clearly explained in the application for approval and relating documents.

When the type approval will be granted applying the condition above, a statement in paragraph 9.1.3. of the communication form (see Annex 1) will inform that the device shall only be installed in a pair.
The reversing lamp shall emit light of the colour white.

The light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.

When visual examination of a reversing lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement referred to above shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 30 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
The operation of direction indicator lamps shall be done in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent).
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall consist of a four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The retro-reflective device shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.

In case of retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F, the retro-reflective device shall bear an orientation mark "TOP" on any marking material whose retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational.

In case of retro-reflective marking plates of Class 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the part of the plates which is intended to be the highest part of the plate when mounted on the vehicle.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4 shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
The approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
The retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The retro-reflective device shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not be rough.
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflective device when in normal use.
The retro-reflecting optical unit shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1=β2= 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1 shall be used.

When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

When verifying the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.

When verifying the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall be examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 =β2 = 0° or if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall be kept by the laboratories for any further checks which may be found necessary.
Four samples out of the remaining eight samples shall be selected at random and divided into two groups of two in each group.

The other eight samples shall be divided into four groups of two: First group: The two samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The other eight samples shall be divided into four groups of two: Second group: The two samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.

The other eight samples shall be divided into four groups of two: Third group: The two samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The other eight samples shall be divided into four groups of two: Fourth group: The two samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the verification of the retro-reflectors shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°.

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., if necessary, the verification of the retro-reflectors shall be performed in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

When applying for approval, the applicant shall specify one or more or a range of axis of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI.

In the case where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.

For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter for Class IA or IB shall be considered.
For photometric measurements, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm².
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area to be used for photometric measurements.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the retro-reflector shall have RI values for red equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for white equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for amber equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IIIA, IIIB white equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IIIA, IIIB amber equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IIIA, IIIB red equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IV white equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IV amber equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The retro-reflector shall have RI values for Class IV red equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The retro-reflector shall not have RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) or (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

When a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the retro-reflector shall have RI values verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The retro-reflector shall be tested for colour (night-time colour) according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The retro-reflector shall have trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', the retro-reflective device shall be rotated about its axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
When the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to this value of ε.
If the specified values are not attained, the retro-reflective device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat test, the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
The retro-reflective device shall not exhibit cracking or appreciable distortion of the optical component after the heat resistance test.
The retro-reflective device shall be stripped of all removable parts before immersion testing.

The retro-reflective device shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
The test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The sample units shall be immediately immersed in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C after the previous test.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
The device shall not be considered to have passed the test if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water.
The RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 of this Regulation, after the retro-reflective device has been lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
The device shall have all drain holes and other openings remain open.
When used, the drain wicks shall be tested in the device.

When the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
After having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4.

The retro-reflective device shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
The resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The retro-reflective areas shall have a coefficient of retro-reflection RA, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', which shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
The surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist before measuring.
The RI shall be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.

The retro-reflective device shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface shall be inspected visually after about five minutes.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned after about 5 minutes.
The RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be fitted so that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
The reference axis of the side retro-reflectors and of side-marker lamps shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
The reference axis of all other signalling devices shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
A tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed in each direction for the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
The rear lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.
In the case where an AFS is installed, the rear lamp shall be verified with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
The requirement for lamps constituting a pair to have substantially identical photometric characteristics shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

When stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
The requirements for single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a) shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.
The rear lamp shall have its maximum height above the ground measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
The rear lamp shall have its minimum height above the ground measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
Where the (maximum and minimum) height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light.
In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF.
In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function.
In the absence of specific instructions, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a rear lamp shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

When viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp.

When viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp towards the rear of a vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The main-beam headlamp shall emit white light.
The dipped-beam headlamp shall emit white light.
The front fog lamp shall emit white or selective yellow light.
The reversing lamp shall emit white light.
The direction-indicator lamp shall emit amber light.
The hazard warning signal shall emit amber light.
The stop lamp shall emit red light.
The emergency stop signal shall emit amber or red light.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall emit amber light.
The rear registration plate lamp shall emit white light.
The front position lamp shall emit white light.
The rear position lamp shall emit red light.
The rear fog lamp shall emit red light.
The parking lamp shall emit white light in front and red light at the rear, or amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The side-marker lamp shall emit amber light, except that the rearmost side-marker lamp may be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The end-outline marker lamp shall emit white light in front and red light at the rear.
The daytime running lamp shall emit white light.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall emit red light.
The rear retro-reflector, triangular, shall emit red light.
The front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall emit light identical to incident light.

The side retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall emit amber light, except that the rearmost side retro-reflector may be red if it is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, the rear end outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop-lamp, the red rearmost side-marker lamp or the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular.
The cornering lamp shall emit white light.
The conspicuity marking shall emit white light to the front and white or yellow light to the side.
The rear conspicuity marking shall emit red or yellow light.
The rear lamp system shall have a number of lamps equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied.

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), additional lamps for the above functions may be switched ON, when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided that these additional lamps satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, with the exception of direction indicator lamps, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, with the exception of direction indicator lamps, the inwards geometric visibility requirement(s) is(are) deemed to be satisfied if this(these) interdependent lamp(s) still conform(s) to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, for direction indicator lamps, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

When the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, where additional lamps are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, photometric and colorimetric requirements applicable to the direction indicator lamps installed on the movable component.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

In the case of dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, when the movable components are moved and returned to the normal position 10 times, no value of the angular inclination of these lamps, relative to its support, measured after each operation of the movable component, shall differ by more than 0.15 per cent from the average of the 10 measured values.

If the limit specified in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1. is exceeded by the value of the angular inclination of dipped-beam headlamps or front fog lamps relative to its support, each limit specified in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1. shall be modified by this excess to decrease the allowed range of inclinations when checking the vehicle according to Annex 6.

When the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of additional lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by a movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the above indicated lamps shall be switched ON.

A remark in the communication form (item 10.1. of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components.

A notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
During replacement of a rear position lamp, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.
During replacement of a rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, which respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed, provided that: (a) The intensity of the all lamps mentioned above, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
In the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

The devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. above shall not be supplied with a voltage exceeding the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity.
No account is taken of obstacles, if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
If measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
Especially in case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle which is approved according to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only.
This requirement does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except for when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
The reversing lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
The reversing lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle.

If installed, the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. may be fitted on the side of the vehicle, provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. below are fulfilled.
When Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the angle α shall be 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
When Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle and if there is only one device, the angle β shall be 45° to right and to left.
When Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle and if there are two devices, the angle β shall be 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

The reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either of the above conditions is not satisfied.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the S1 or S2 stop lamp devices that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For all other categories of vehicles, the S1 or S2 stop lamp devices shall have a distance in between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of not less than 600 mm.

For all other categories of vehicles, the distance in between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the S1 or S2 stop lamp devices in the direction of the reference axes may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
For S3 or S4 stop lamp devices, the centre of reference shall be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
In the case where the two S3 or S4 stop lamp devices are installed, they shall be positioned as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane, one on each side of this plane.

In the case where one S3 or S4 stop lamp device offset from the median longitudinal plane is permitted according to paragraph 6.7.2., the offset shall not exceed 150 mm from the median longitudinal plane to the centre of reference of the lamp.
For S1 or S2 stop lamp devices, the height above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm.

For S1 or S2 stop lamp devices, if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed, the height above the ground may be increased to 2,100 mm.
If the optional stop lamp devices are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.
If the optional stop lamp devices are installed, they shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible.
If the optional stop lamp devices are installed, they shall be positioned at a height not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The stop lamp shall be not more than 150 mm below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the exposed surface of the glass or glazing of the rear window, except that for S3 or S4 categories devices the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall either not be more than 150 mm below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the exposed surface of the glass or glazing of the rear window, or not be less than 850 mm above the ground.

The stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of S1 or S2 categories devices, except that for S3 or S4 categories devices the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of S1 or S2 categories devices.
The stop lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices the stop lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle.

The stop lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices the horizontal angle shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

The stop lamp shall have an inward horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The stop lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 10° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for S3 or S4 categories devices the horizontal angle shall be 10° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
The stop lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices the vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.

The stop lamp shall have a downward vertical angle of 15°, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

The stop lamp shall have an upward vertical angle of 15°, except that for S1 or S2 categories devices where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The stop lamp shall have a vertical angle of 10° above and 5° below the horizontal, except that for S3 or S4 categories devices the vertical angle shall be 10° above and 5° below the horizontal.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
The stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The rear position lamp shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle in width, except that this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.
The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes for M1 and N1 category vehicles shall have no special requirement.
The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes for all other categories of vehicles shall be not less than 600 mm.
The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The rear position lamp shall be not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground.
The rear position lamp shall be not more than 2,100 mm above the ground if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the symmetry of the lamps.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres to be considered visible.
The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded when determining the unobstructed view.
The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
The rear position lamp shall have electrical connections in accordance with paragraph 5.11.

If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
A closed-circuit tell-tale shall be mandatory for the rear position lamp.
The closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamp shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
The requirement for a closed-circuit tell-tale does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
A tell-tale indicating failure shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular shall be provided that they are grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.
Rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular shall be optional on trailers.

The rear retro-reflector shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4. below) shall be permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle in width.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 900 mm above the ground.
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 1,200 mm above the ground if grouped with any rear lamp(s).
The rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 1,500 mm above the ground if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively.
The rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle in length.
The rear retro-reflector shall have a horizontal angle of visibility of 30° inwards and outwards.
The rear retro-reflector shall have a vertical angle of visibility of 10° above and below horizontal.
Where a rear retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of visibility may be reduced to 5°.
The rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
The sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
In case of an ESA being (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, granted to this ESA.

In case of an ESA being (part of) a light source, the applicant shall provide a test report by a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority, stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation.

The vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, a minimum of 25 volts/m shall be present over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, a minimum of 8 volts/m shall be present over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
If tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, a minimum of 50 mA shall be present over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the rear lamp shall be not more than 62 dB microvolts/m and not less than 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the rear lamp shall have a limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the rear lamp shall be not more than 52 dB microvolts/m and not less than 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the rear lamp shall have a limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the rear lamp shall be not more than 63 dB microvolts/m and not less than 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the rear lamp shall have measured values expressed in dB microvolts/m below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the rear lamp shall be not more than 52 dB microvolts/m and not less than 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the rear lamp shall have a limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the rear lamp shall be not more than 42 dB microvolts/m and not less than 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the rear lamp shall have a limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the rear lamp shall be not more than 53 dB microvolts/m and not less than 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.

The test severity for the frequency range below 2 GHz in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be not less than 60 V/m for Stripline TEM cell, not less than 75 V/m for BCI ALSE, not less than 60 mA for Reverberation chamber, and not less than 30 V/m for Frequency range below 2 GHz.
The test severity for the frequency range above 2 GHz in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be not less than 21 V/m for Frequency range below 2 GHz.

The test severity for the frequency range above 2 GHz in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be not less than 10 V/m for Stripline TEM cell, not less than Not applicable for BCI ALSE, not less than Not applicable for Reverberation chamber, and not less than 7 V/m for Frequency range above 2 GHz.

The minimum test severity for the frequency range above 2 GHz over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be not less than 8 V/m for Stripline TEM cell, not less than Not applicable for BCI ALSE, not less than Not applicable for Reverberation chamber, and not less than 6 V/m for Frequency range above 2 GHz.

The ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
If not otherwise stated in this Annex, the test shall be performed according CISPR 25.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
ESAs involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be in charging mode.
The state of charge (SOC) of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement.
If the test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA shall be tested at rated current.
If the current consumption can be adjusted, then the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

If the current consumption can be adjusted, then the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its nominal value or to a minimum of 16 A (if the 20 per cent of its nominal value cannot be achieved in the test facility) for DC charging unless another value is agreed with the type approval authorities.
The limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The rear lamp shall be tested in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
When tested in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
When tested in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs.
When tested in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs.
If not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer, the frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1, throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz.

If the manufacturer provides measurement to data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025, and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may choose a reduced number of spot frequencies in the range (e.g. 27, 45, 65, 90, 120, 150, 190, 230, 280, 380, 450, 600, 750, 900, 1,300, 1,800, 2,360, 2,600, 3,000, 3,600, 5,200 and 5,900 MHz) to confirm that the ESA meets the requirements of this Annex.
The rear lamp shall be subjected to immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines.

The test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b shall be applied according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The starting profile shall be applied according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to starting profile.
The rear lamp shall be measured for emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2.
